- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in subsequent periods; dampen forecast by 2–5% for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.00 or -0.33), model underperforms; apply upward bias of 2–4% to counteract mean reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags behind true price by 1–2 days; adjust forecast to match recent 7–14 day moving average if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in the following 3–5 periods to reflect sentiment reversal.
